mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: lower rates predict positive 20-day returns due to compressed discount rates on equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20d returns < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points signals labor market deterioration, triggering negative 5-day S&P 500 returns through reduced consumer spending confidence.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE rises >0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) and fall in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an inflationary supply shock, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns through reduced corporate margins.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2% in 1 month AND INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises >0.2% and INDPRO falls >0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When annualized CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, central bank tightening leads to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns through reduced liquidity and higher risk premiums.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation >3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Higher real GDP levels (GDPC1) predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days due to stronger corporate earnings visibility and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: Rank IC between GDPC1 and 20d returns < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month fall in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1.0% signals economic weakness, triggering negative 5-day S&P 500 returns through reduced manufacturing activity.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns positive in >60% of instances when INDPRO falls >1.0% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) and fall in consumer spending (RSAFS) signals an inflationary demand shock, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns through reduced purchasing power.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2% in 1 month AND RSAFS falls > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises >0.2% and RSAFS falls >0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.5%, weak consumer spending leads to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns through reduced corporate revenue growth expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE >5.5%.
